pull.title: refactor(rotation): consolidate provider and websearch engines into core
pull.body:
## What

One parameterized RotationEngine in core/credential_rotation.py now serves both key pools. Every historical point of divergence between the provider engine (async, SDK-classified failures) and the websearch KeyPool (sync, caller-classified) is a RotationTuning field; PROVIDER_TUNING and WEBSEARCH_TUNING reproduce both engines' documented behavior exactly. providers/credential_rotation.py keeps SDK failure classification on top; websearch/rotation.py becomes a thin adapter carrying key material, masking, and admin snapshots. parse_websearch_keys deleted in favor of parse_credential_keys; admin_routes rewired to surviving symbols.

Closes the "two rotation engines" structural debt item.

## Verification

ruff/format/check + ty clean; provider suite 21 passed, websearch suite 26 passed — both exercising the shared engine through their historical public APIs unchanged. Storage-hygiene companion commits (bb474e9, 19597c8) already on this branch carry their own 37-test suite + 4 caught-by-name mutations.

## Residual risks

Behavioral parity is pinned by the two historical suites; any undocumented divergence between engines would surface as a test failure here rather than in production.

## Follow-up fix (c5ee5e1)

Linux CI caught three behavioral divergences between the consolidated engine and both historical pools; all three fixed on this branch and re-verified green:

1. refresh() re-woke already-awake HALF_OPEN slots on every choose(), clearing an outstanding probe reservation (unlimited probe admission). It now skips any slot already in the wake state.
2. In both historical pools the lockouts counter doubles as the live escalation index (backoff keyed off it, success zeroed it). Recovery now resets it alongside auth_failures instead of preserving a lifetime total.
3. KeyPool.health_at() returned point-in-time snapshots where the old pool handed out its own mutable record; ported tests hold references across transitions. KeyHealth is now a live-backed facade over the engine slot with an identical attribute surface; snapshot/dashboard payload shapes unchanged.

Fix verification: whole suites green locally (providers rotation + websearch rotation + websearch analytics = 112 passed), ruff format/check + ty clean, suites re-run green post-rebase. Version bumped to 5.57.0 in-branch (MINOR: wave-6 stream-recovery observability tiles land with this PR).

commit.message:
fix(websearch): reclaim pruned pages via incremental auto-vacuum

Port requests.db's auto_vacuum pattern into websearch analytics schema
init: _ensure_auto_vacuum adopts INCREMENTAL on fresh databases and
performs a one-time VACUUM+ANALYZE rebuild of existing auto_vacuum=0
installs; _prune drains freed pages back to the filesystem via
PRAGMA incremental_vacuum. Row-based retention is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(websearch): drain incremental vacuum cursor and pin rebuild contract

An unconsumed PRAGMA incremental_vacuum cursor leaves the statement
suspended after its first step, so every prune reclaimed a single page
while the rest of the freed pages stayed on the freelist; consume the
pragma's rows so row-cap pruning actually returns bytes to the
filesystem. Pin _ensure_auto_vacuum's contract with real-connection
trace-callback tests (single probe statement when already INCREMENTAL;
legacy databases convert via PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL, VACUUM,
ANALYZE under autocommit and restore the prior isolation level),
replacing a duck-typed fake that crashed on fetchone and tripped ty's
argument-type check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(rotation): consolidate provider and websearch engines into core

One parameterized RotationEngine in core/credential_rotation.py now
serves both key pools: health states, cooldown/lockout ladders, circuit
breaker, half-open probe admission, and selection policies exist once;
every historical point of divergence is a RotationTuning field
(PROVIDER_TUNING / WEBSEARCH_TUNING reproduce both engines' documented
behavior exactly). providers/credential_rotation.py keeps SDK failure
classification on top; websearch/rotation.py becomes a thin adapter
carrying key material, masking, and admin snapshots. parse_websearch_keys
is deleted in favor of parse_credential_keys; admin_routes rewired to
the surviving symbols (mask_credential_label).

Verified: ruff/format/check + ty clean; provider suite 21 passed,
websearch suite 26 passed (whole files); both suites exercise the shared
engine through their historical public APIs unchanged.

fix(rotation): rename circuit_open_threshold to circuit_threshold

The consolidated RotationEngine uses circuit_threshold; every caller
(tests, runtime/config.py, runtime/factory.py) still passed the old
provider-engine kwarg name, causing 36 TypeErrors across Linux CI.
Mechanical rename; no behavior change.

feat(observability): per-attempt stream-recovery counters with dashboard tiles

The provider's transparent recovery -- early retries, midstream
continuations, tool salvages -- left no trace in the request log: a
request that survived several invisible upstream failures looked
identical to one served first try. RecoveryController already owned the
decisions, but they died inside the stream runner while the log row is
finalized at the API boundary.

A per-request RecoveryTrace collector bridges the two the same way
credential attribution does: request_capture installs it once per logged
request, the openai_chat runner records at each recovery seam (the
early-retry branch, a successful continuation, both salvage points), and
set_routing re-buckets the collector at every attempt boundary so events
land on the chain index that earned them. Counters persist as a guarded
params JSON column on request_attempts -- NULL on rows written before
counting existed, which reads as unmeasured, not zero -- aggregate
through stats() into a recovery block tolerant of unreadable blobs, and
surface as three dashboard tiles beside the fallback figures. Tests
cover migration without data loss, store round-trip, filtered
aggregates, capture bucketing across attempts, provider-seam recording,
and jsdom tile rendering; mutation checks confirm every new guard fails
its named test when broken.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(rotation): restore historical probe, lockout-reset, and live-view contracts

The consolidated RotationEngine reproduced both pools' ladders and
thresholds but diverged from their observable contracts in three ways,
red on Linux CI:

1. refresh() skipped only HEALTHY slots, so a HALF_OPEN slot whose stale
   deadline had passed was re-woken on every choose(), clearing an
   outstanding probe reservation and admitting unlimited probes. The old
   provider sweep transitioned only LOCKED_OUT/COOLDOWN/CIRCUIT_OPEN and
   left awake HALF_OPEN slots untouched. refresh() now skips slots already
   in the wake state (identical behavior for websearch, whose wake state
   is HEALTHY itself).

2. _clear_benching() preserved a lifetime lockouts total. In both
   historical pools the counter doubled as the LIVE escalation index -
   backoff keyed off it and success zeroed it ("a later success resets
   the escalation") - so recovery now resets it alongside auth_failures.

3. KeyPool.health_at() returned fresh point-in-time snapshots where the
   historical pool handed out its own mutable record; ported tests hold
   a reference across further transitions and assert through it
   (state_until froze at 300.0/0.0 instead of tracking the ladder).
   KeyHealth is now a live-backed facade over the engine slot with the
   same attribute surface; snapshot/dashboard payload shapes unchanged.

Verification: whole suites green locally - tests/providers/
test_credential_rotation.py plus tests/websearch/test_rotation.py plus
tests/websearch/test_analytics.py = 112 passed; ruff format/check clean;
uv run ty check clean. The three previously-red tests pass by name.

Not done: provider-side metrics never exposed lockouts, so no consumer
changes there; admin snapshot keys unchanged.

Version: 5.57.0 (MINOR - wave 6 adds stream-recovery observability tiles
alongside this consolidation).
